en: to make something steady and less likely to change or fall; to become steady and not change; to keep a patient's condition from getting worse
n. a violent weather condition with strong winds and rain, thunder or snow; a sudden strong reaction; v. to attack a place suddenly and violently; to move in a very angry way
n. a legal document ordering someone to appear in court or to produce evidence; v. to order someone by law to appear in court or give evidence
to experience something unpleasant, such as pain, loss or hardship; to be badly affected by something; to bear or tolerate
to use force to stop something; to stop yourself from doing something or showing a feeling; to prevent information from being published or known
a doctor who is trained to perform operations; (in the navy) an officer who is a doctor
the sending of messages over long distances by telephone, radio, television or the internet; the technology and business of doing this
a set of ideas or principles that explains why something happens or exists; the general principles of a subject; an opinion or idea

v. to move an organ or tissue from one body to another; to move a plant to another place; to move people from one place to another; n. the process of transplanting; an organ that has been transplanted
medical care given to a patient for an illness or injury; the way in which someone behaves toward or deals with another person or thing; a process of dealing with something
the highest social class, consisting of wealthy and powerful people; the group of people in a country with the highest social status

n. the usefulness or importance of something; a principle or standard of behavior; the amount of money something is worth; v. to consider something to be important; to estimate the monetary worth of something
a very small living thing that can cause disease in people, animals or plants; (computing) a program that damages the information on a computer
n. useless or unwanted material that is thrown away; a bad use of time, money or effort; v. to use something carelessly or in a way that does not give good results
n. the business of selling goods in large quantities at low prices to businesses; a. relating to the selling of goods in large quantities; complete and without limits; adv. in large quantities
a public show of paintings, products or other things; the act of showing a skill or quality
ex: The museum opened a new photography exhibition last week.
博物館上週開了一個新的攝影展。

en: n. a tool with a long handle and a broad blade for digging or moving material; v. to dig or move something with a shovel
ex: He used a shovel to clear the snow from the driveway.
他用鏟子清掉車道上的積雪。

en: the narrow part of the body between the ribs and the hips; the part of a piece of clothing that fits around this area
ex: She tied a ribbon around her waist before the party.
她在派對前在腰間繫了一條緞帶。

en: n. an act of traveling from one place to another, especially a long one; a process of change or development; v. to travel from one place to another
ex: The journey from Taipei to Kaohsiung takes about two hours by high-speed rail.
從台北到高雄搭高鐵約兩小時。

en: important or large enough to have an effect or to be noticed; having a particular meaning; (of statistics) unlikely to have occurred by chance
ex: There has been a significant increase in sales since January.
自一月以來銷售額有顯著成長。

en: to send a file or data from your computer to a server or the internet; (n.) a file that has been sent in this way
ex: Please upload the report to the shared folder before noon.
請在中午前把報告上傳到共用資料夾。

en: n. a sudden bright light that lasts for a short time; a sudden flash of insight; a very short time; v. to shine suddenly and briefly; to appear or pass quickly; to reflect light
ex: A flash of lightning lit up the whole sky.
一道閃電照亮了整片天空。

en: a place where films are shown; the art or business of making films
ex: We went to the cinema to see the new action movie.
我們去電影院看了新的動作片。

en: a. honest and direct in speech, even if it is unpleasant; v. to stamp mail with a mark so that it can be sent free; n. (US) a hot dog
ex: To be frank, I don't think the plan will work.
老實說，我不認為這個計畫行得通。

en: a large farm building used for storing grain, hay or equipment, and sometimes for keeping animals
ex: The farmer stored the hay in the barn for the winter.
農夫把乾草存放在穀倉裡過冬。

en: v. to gradually lose color, strength or importance; to become faint; to gradually disappear; n. a gradual disappearance of an image or sound
ex: The colors on the old poster have faded over the years.
這張舊海報的顏色這些年來已經褪色了。

en: n. a narrow line of light or other radiation; a small amount of something; (fish) a flat sea creature with a long tail; v. to send out rays of light; to shine
ex: A ray of sunlight shone through the window.
一道陽光從窗戶照進來。

en: a team game in which two teams hit a large ball over a high net with their hands; the ball used in this game
ex: We play volleyball on the beach every summer.
我們每年夏天都在海灘上打排球。

en: relating to electronic equipment such as computers, or using small electronic circuits; (of music) produced or played using electronic devices
ex: Many students read electronic books on their tablets.
許多學生用平板閱讀電子書。

en: n. the importance or usefulness of something; the money value of something; a. having a particular value; deserving a particular action or treatment
ex: This old watch is worth a lot of money.
這隻舊手錶價值不菲。

en: prep. on top of or touching something; at the moment of or immediately after something happening; depending on or based on something; when something happens to someone
ex: Once upon a time, there lived a king in a faraway land.
從前，在遙遠的國度住著一位國王。

en: a. strange or unusual in an uncomfortable way; (n./a.) a term for sexual or gender identities outside heterosexual and cisgender norms, once an insult but now also used by those communities themselves
ex: There was something queer about the way he kept looking over his shoulder.
他不斷回頭張望的樣子有點古怪。

en: a. feeling frightened or worried; (formal) very bad or serious; causing fear
ex: The children were fearful of the dark forest at night.
孩子們很害怕夜晚的暗黑森林。

en: to help something to develop or be successful; to give someone a higher job or rank; to advertise something so that people want to buy it; to start something such as a business
ex: The company decided to promote her to regional manager.
公司決定把她升為區域經理。

en: a large open-air or covered structure where sports events and concerts are held, with seating for spectators
ex: Thousands of fans filled the stadium to watch the final match.
數千名球迷擠滿體育場觀看決賽。

en: a. spoken rather than written; relating to the mouth; n. an examination in which questions are asked and answered aloud
ex: The students have to pass an oral test in English next week.
學生們下週必須通過英文口試。

en: the study of the earth's surface, including its physical features, climate, population and resources; the physical features of a particular place
ex: She loves studying geography and dreams of visiting every continent.
她熱愛地理學，夢想遊遍每一個大陸。

en: n. a series of musical notes that make a recognizable song; the correct musical pitch; v. to adjust a musical instrument so that it produces the right notes; to adjust a radio to receive a particular station; to adjust an engine
ex: The musician spent an hour tuning his guitar before the concert.
音樂家在演奏會前花了一小時調他的吉他。

en: a. (of weather) covered with thick mist or fog; unclear or confused in the mind
ex: The morning was so foggy that we could hardly see the road.
那天早上霧很濃，我們幾乎看不清路。

en: to become wider or make something wider; to increase the range or scope of something
ex: The government plans to widen the highway to reduce traffic jams.
政府計畫拓寬這條公路以減少塞車。
